chunks: He said: Then he (peace be upon him) wiped his hand over his noble, honored beard, and wept for a long time, then he said (peace be upon him):
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali do before speaking about the Mahdi in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this poignant scene from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) demonstrates the profound emotional depth of the Ahl al-Bayt by wiping his beard—a gesture of contemplation and humility—before weeping, likely reflecting on the trials of his lineage or the impending rise of al-Mahdi. This act underscores the Shia scholarly view that the Imams' tears are not merely signs of sorrow but expressions of *huzn* (spiritual grief) for the suffering of the Ummah and the weight of divine trust. It serves as a powerful reminder of the human yet divinely guided nature of the Imams, bridging historical narrative with spiritual introspection.
